text:
dev-rel: Quick announcement — we just published Community Model Zoo v1.0: curated inference recipes, eval harnesses, and tiny tooling to make onboarding open models easier. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-model-zoo :tada:

release-bot: Published release v1.0.0 · tag: v1.0.0 · commit: abc1234def — changelog added.

alisha: woo! what's the license for the artifacts in the repo?

dev-rel: Most adapter code and recipes are MIT. Model weights follow upstream model licenses (see LICENSES.md in the repo). We added a LICENSE_SUMMARY.md with quick mapping.

chris: Any notes for running locally or in Dedicated? migration concerns?

dev-rel: No breaking API changes. Quick start: `pip install redwood-cmz==1.0.0` then:
```
redwood-cmz run --recipe llama-7b-ptq --backend dedicated --pool my-dedicated-pool
```
Recipes live under /recipes; evals under /evals. If you're using custom routing policies, make sure to pin model_variant in the recipe.

maya: Ops question — some recipes pull cached weights from s3. Can we add bandwidth guards? worried about big pulls during scale tests.

dev-rel: Good catch. Added a note in the README about staging artifacts and a `--no-fetch` flag for local tests. Ops, we've also added a runbook snippet to limit concurrent fetches to 3 per-worker (see infra/runbooks).

alisha: planning to surface this in the community maintainer rotation doc? would help deflect basic Qs.

dev-rel: Yep — created a PR to add a CMZ section in the maintainer playbook and listed initial maintainers: @alisha, @chris, @maya. Also hosting a 30min community office hours: Thu 10:00am PT — drop by to walk through recipes and contribution workflow. Calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/community-cmz

chris: I'll try the PTQ recipe tomorrow and share perf numbers (latency, tokens/sec).

alisha: :tada: congrats team, will share on socials after the office hours.

release-bot: Noting: security-scan passed for release v1.0.0 (no critical findings).

dev-rel: Thanks—if anyone finds issues, open an issue in the repo and tag the `cmz-maintainers` label. Appreciate the early testers! :heart:
